Subject: Re: Ausmus 
 
Thanks. Safe travels to Minny

On Fri, Sep 11, 2015 at 7:15 PM, Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com> wrote:
Yeah, I talked to Al this morning. Since then, it’s been business as usual.
Nothing’s changed from when he was hired.
Reports sting you? Not really.
Awkward? For who? You. Not really.

Feel like a lame duck manager? Not at all, these guys will continue to play the game the right way and people want to make a big deal about that and often, managers use it in the final year of a contract to try and get an extension but the truth is, the players will respect you or not respect you regardless of what your contract status is.
Have you thought about it today? It’s hard not to think about it but I certainly haven’t been dwelling on it.

Ever consider not wanting to come back? No, I have a contract and I will do everything I can to help the tigers until they tell me they don’t want me to help them or until the contract expires, whichever comes first.
Any consideration to ask Al to move up eval process? No, I’m very comfortable with where everything is right now.
Told anything about your future? “I think Al’s statement covered it.”

What’s been the most trying part of this year? “You.” Second to me, it can’t be me. No, it’s not you. I just think going into the trading deadline we dind’t have the record we thought we wanted to have or should have had but that being said, we were still very much in the hunt.

About realities of managing, losing jobs: “I still haven’t hung pictures up on my wall in the office. Very few managers end up walking away from the job, they’re usually told to walk away and even when they’re not fired, they’re often just not rehired so trust me, I’m aware of that nad I’ve been aware of that since I’ve been a player.”
Anybody reach out? “I’ve had people reach out to me but obviously that’s personal, I wouldn’t discuss that.”
Want to be back next year? “Yeah, absolutely.”
How confident are you that you will be back? “I’m not going to put odds on it, I don’t want there to be betting.”

Playing career help with the scrutiny? “Well, I didn’t get a lot of this. There’s not as much focus on, there wasn’t much focus on me as a player, I wasn’t a primetime player, I was a piece of a puzzle on a team. I’ve certainly been booed at times as a player but you don’t worry about that. Being booed isn’t necessarily bad because it just shows that the fans care. I’d rather be fans in the seats booing me than not showing up.”
All communication with Al or has there been any communication with ownership? “I wouldn’t get into that but I spoke to Al today.”
Report out of the blue? “I hadn’t heard anything so I guess the answer would be yes, it was.”

How did you find out? “I got a couple texts last night saying that Bernie was breaking some story and people wanted to know what it was and I had no idea, quite frankly, so I found out the same way everybody else did.”

Concerning that there are different voices within the organization? “The anonymous source? I love anonymous sources, they don’t have quite the spine to put their name next to their words. That’s coming from above me, that’s not really my concern. My concern is my clubhouse and on the field. I’m not worried if there’s multiple voices coming from above me, I can’t control that.”

Ever been in a situation like this as player with manager on hot seat? “It happened with Jimy Williams, he was let go midseason and I felt to blame as a player. It wasn’t Jimy’s fault that at the time, the Astros were underperforming. It was a little odd, and I felt for Jimy, I called him when they fired him because I felt responsible.”
Anthony Fenech
